findings.problem: In the section only the west corner post visibly reaches the ground; the posts along the front rim joist stop at the underside of the rim joist with open space below, so the outer edge of the 12 m deck (and the porch posts' point loads on the east half) shows no continuous support to the ground.
findings.evidence: view_deck_under.png: the corner post at the left runs down beside the lattice, while the middle and right posts end at the rim joist bottom; the wall-side ledger is not distinguishable in the shadow band at the wall, so the inner end is not shown either. Plan: SkirtPosts are 'corner posts' only.
findings.fix: Add ground-reaching 4x4/6x6 posts under the front rim joist about every 2 to 2.4 m (hidden behind the lattice), one directly under each porch post, and make the wall ledger readable in a close-up (cedar board on the wall at joist height, joists meeting it).

findings.problem: The long vertical run down the gable wall shows no straps or brackets, so it reads as held only at the gutter.
findings.evidence: view_eave.png: the rose-brown pipe from the corner elbow down to the bottom of the frame is a plain continuous tube with no clips; the building guidance asks for a long downspout to be strapped to the wall.
findings.fix: Add two or three small rose-brown band straps (a thin ring plus a short tab to the siding) along each downspout, one near the top and one every 1.2 to 1.5 m.

findings.problem: The gutter's end at the gable corner has no clean end cap: a small jagged white notch breaks the top edge where the rake board's lower end meets the gutter.
findings.evidence: view_eave.png: near the top of the outlet, at the corner board, the gutter's top edge shows a small zigzag step.
findings.fix: Give the gutter a closed end cap that stops just short of the rake board end, and keep the rake board's lower end plumb and clear of the gutter.

features.evidence: view_steps_side.png: the stair side is a stepped cedar profile with a sloped underside, its top meeting the deck rim joist and its low end standing on the ground, with treads and risers running into each other down to the ground; the sheet's stringer section agrees.

view_deck_under.png: joists run from the front rim joist back to the wall and a corner post reaches the ground, but the mid-span posts end at the rim joist underside and the wall ledger cannot be told apart in the shadow, so the full path to the ground is not shown.

view_garden.png: the porch roof's back edge meets the wall under the upper windows and its front edge has a white beam resting on three posts that stand on the deck (left, middle and right); sheet 'Doors and porch' shows the same.

view_eave.png shows the outlet leaving the gutter end, the offset elbow across the corner board and the plumb run down the gable wall, but the foot and any splash block are outside the frame; only the 4-point route gate covers the end.

findings.problem: The porch posts stand on the decking surface, so the roof load would bear on deck boards instead of going down through a joist or post to the ground.
findings.evidence: Plan line PorchPosts -> Decking; the 'Deck: railing, lattice, step' close-up shows the post base sitting on the boards, with no visible blocking or footing.
findings.fix: Land each porch post on a rim joist or a doubled joist, or on a block that runs through the decking to a skirt post or footing, and cut the decking around the post base.

findings.problem: The downspout is about 6 m long and shows no straps or brackets, so it looks held only at the gutter end.
findings.evidence: 'Eave corner: gutter, downspout' close-up: a plain tube from the elbow down the wall with no bands.
findings.fix: Add two or three thin strap bands, rose-brown like the pipe, that wrap the pipe and touch the wall or corner board at roughly 1.5 m spacing.

findings.problem: The sliding double sashes show no latch or meeting-rail hardware, so the windows read as fixed glass in a casing.
findings.evidence: 'Upper floor window' and 'Ground floor window sill' close-ups show only the casing and a plain meeting rail.
findings.fix: Add a small sash latch on the meeting rail, or accept that the windows are not meant to be used.

features.evidence: Only the front of the step is visible in 'Deck: railing, lattice, step'. The stringers, their notches and the deck-frame connection are hidden from every view.
The lattice skirt hides the posts and the joists, and the wall ledger is not visible in any view, so the support under the deck cannot be judged from the renders.
The garden facade view and the 'Deck' and 'Doors and porch' close-ups show the porch roof meeting the wall at its high side, with white posts under a beam at the front edge.

The 'Eave corner' close-up shows the gutter ending in an elbow and a downspout running down the wall. The lower end and the splash block are out of frame in every view, so the 'ends over a splash block' part cannot be seen.

findings.problem: The outer edge of a roughly 12 m long deck is carried only by the guessed 'corner posts of the deck skirt'; no view shows posts or piers at intervals under the rim joist, nor the ledger and joists, so the outer load path to the ground is not demonstrated.
findings.evidence: Plan rows SkirtPosts ('corner posts', guess) and DeckFrame ('guess'); the section view 'what carries the deck's outer edge' shows only a thin rim band with small white elements, no joists, ledger or footings; deck x -4.2..7.8 in the generator's notes.
findings.fix: Add posts or piers under the rim joist at roughly 1.5-2.4 m spacing (doubled or beam-style rim), footed on the ground and hidden behind the lattice, and add a cutaway view that shows the ledger, joists and posts.

findings.problem: The porch posts stand on the decking, so the porch roof load would pass through deck boards and the guessed deck frame instead of reaching their own footings.
findings.evidence: Plan row PorchPosts ('standing on the decking', attached to Decking); 'Doors and porch' and 'Deck: railing, lattice, step' views show posts sitting on the deck surface.
findings.fix: Land each porch post directly over a rim joist or a post/pier running down to the ground (e.g. a post continuing through the deck, or blocking plus a pier under it), and attach it to DeckFrame as well as Decking.

findings.problem: No strap or bracket is distinguishable on the long downspout run down the gable wall, so it appears held only at the gutter.
findings.evidence: 'Eave corner: gutter, downspout' view shows a plain pipe running down the wall; the building guidance asks for a long downspout to be strapped to the wall.
findings.fix: Add two or three small pipe straps (rose-brown bands screwed to the siding) along each downspout, one near the top, one at mid-height and one near the splash block.

features.evidence: steps_side is shot from above and shows treads and risers with wood grain; the notched stringers underneath are not visible in any view.
deck_under (section view) is too small to show the ledger on the wall, the joists or posts at the outer edge; only a thin rim band and small white elements are visible.
garden and 'Doors and porch' views show the porch roof meeting the wall above the ground-floor openings, a white beam under its outer edge and white posts standing on the decking below the beam.

eave view shows the downspout leaving the gutter end and running down the gable wall, but the views cut off before its lower end, so the splash block is not visible (the build's route gate measured pass).
